valuation_philosophy: Liberty Global is NOT a consolidated-FCF DCF story. Consolidated financials cover only Telenet (Belgium), Wyre (Belgian fiber netco), VM Ireland, and Liberty Corporate & Services -- the 50%-owned VMO2 (UK) and VodafoneZiggo (Netherlands, pending full buy-in) JVs are equity-accounted and invisible in consolidated revenue/EBITDA/FCF. Consolidated owner FCF (ex-JV distributions) has been negative-to-breakeven every year FY2023-2025 (-$260M, +$28M, -$450M) due to the Wyre/Telenet fiber capex cycle -- a genuine trough, not a reason to write off the business. This model uses a SUM-OF-THE-PARTS approach: (1) a 10-year component-built owner-FCF DCF on consolidated operations only, capturing the capex normalization management itself guides to (Telenet P&E falling from ~38% to ~20% of revenue as Wyre now carries fiber capex on a separated capital structure); (2) the two 50% JV stakes (VMO2, VodafoneZiggo) valued via EV/EBITDA on their own annualized financials, cross-checked against Liberty Global's equity-method carrying values on the balance sheet (VMO2 $3,481.1M, VodafoneZiggo $1,623.8M at Q2-2026); (3) the Liberty Growth venture/data-center/media portfolio at management's own mark-to-market FMV ($3.4B, ~70 companies); less (4) consolidated net debt and the ~$1.16B cash cost of the pending VodafoneZiggo stake buy-in from Vodafone (expected to close end-July 2026, per Q2-2026 earnings call, after the June 30 2026 balance sheet date used for net debt). The VodafoneZiggo transaction's ~$1B of stated synergies and 2027 Ziggo Group Euronext spin-off are treated as bull-case optionality, not underwritten into the base case, given multiple sequential regulatory/execution steps remain.

inputs.vz_deal_cash_cost_note: EUR 1.0bn (~$1.16bn at ~1.16 EURUSD) cash Liberty Global pays Vodafone for its remaining 50% VodafoneZiggo stake, expected to close end-July 2026 (after the Q2-2026 10-Q balance-sheet date); treated as an incremental use of cash / addition to net debt across all scenarios since it is a near-certain near-term outflow. Liberty Global also issues Vodafone a 10% stake in the new Ziggo Group holding company (Telenet+VodafoneZiggo, ex-Wyre) -- this dilution is NOT separately modeled; it is implicitly conservative since consolidated Telenet is valued at its current 100% economics in this model.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Consolidated operations (Telenet+Wyre+VM Ireland+Corporate) owner FCF, Year 1 of the projection -- EXCLUDES JV cash distributions (valued separately as part of the JV stake blocks) to avoid double-counting. Reported consolidated FY2025 FCF (company definition, per CSV) was -$132.0M; the true OCF-less-capex-less-JV-distributions figure was -$450.1M (see fcf_reconciliation).
inputs.jv_cash_distributions_note: VMO2 JV $245.8M + VodafoneZiggo JV $72.3M dividend distributions actually received in cash during FY2025 (down from $394.3M in FY2024). FY2026 guidance: VMO2 ~$128M (50% of ~£200M), VodafoneZiggo $0 (retained ahead of buyout).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped separately -- LBTYA's net cash position is negative (net debt ~$5.9B) so no phantom double-count risk from corporate interest income. Note $57.7M of VodafoneZiggo-JV-receivable interest income flows into the VZ JV's own results, already reflected in the JV valuation, not in consolidated FCF.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 Note 15 (Share-based Compensation), aggregate Liberty Global SBC per Metrics.csv
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Actual FY2025 share repurchases (10-K MD&A). No 2026 buyback program was authorized until a sharply reduced $200M authorization approved July 2026 (vs. a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar prior program). Buyback cash ($192.1M) modestly exceeded SBC ($169.4M) in FY2025, so uncovered_dilution = $0 and shares are held flat in the projection -- conservative given the 2026 authorization is smaller and buybacks could lag SBC going forward.

fcf_reconciliation.description: Consolidated FCF (ex-JV distributions) is the true measure of consolidated-operations cash generation; it excludes JV dividends (valued separately in the JV stake blocks) to avoid double-counting, per the sum-of-parts methodology.
fcf_reconciliation.notes: Reported FCF (company/CSV definition) is materially higher than consolidated_fcf_ex_jv_distributions because it includes JV cash distributions as an operating inflow. Since this model values the JV stakes separately (sum-of-parts), consolidated_fcf_ex_jv_distributions is the correct base for the consolidated-operations DCF component to avoid double-counting JV value.

historical_growth.revenue_3yr_cagr_note: FY2022 (first full post-Sunrise-spinoff-comparable restated year) to FY2025: ($4,878.5M / $4,017.5M)^(1/3) - 1 = 6.7%. Pre-FY2022 revenue is NOT comparable -- it includes the since-deconsolidated UK (VMO2 JV formation 2021), Swiss (Sunrise spin-off Nov-2024), Polish and other operations, so no 5yr or 10yr revenue CAGR is presented.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: FY2022 $22,573.4M to FY2025 $9,735.7M = -24.4% CAGR. Heavily distorted by the Sunrise spin-off distribution (equity leaves with the spun-off entity, not a value-destroying event) and the FY2025 VodafoneZiggo/VMO2 fair-value writedowns (net loss -$7,138.1M). NOT used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr: Not meaningful -- consolidated FCF (ex-JV distributions) has been negative or near-zero every year FY2023-2025 due to the Wyre/Telenet fiber capex cycle; there is no positive base to compound.
historical_growth.eps_cagr: Not meaningful -- EPS is dominated by non-cash JV fair-value swings and impairments (FY2025 net loss -$20.86/share largely from a $7.1B non-cash charge).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: CRITICAL: Standard historical CAGR selection logic (equity/revenue/EPS) does not apply to LBTYA. Revenue, equity and EPS have all been repeatedly broken by structural deconsolidations (VMO2 2021, Sunrise 2024) and non-cash JV/impairment swings. This model instead builds forward FCF from revenue/margin/capex components anchored to FY2025 actuals and FY2026 segment guidance, and values the JV stakes and Liberty Growth portfolio independently rather than growing a consolidated historical base.
historical_growth.notes: SBC ($169.4M FY2025) grew from $163.2M (FY2022) at a ~1.2% CAGR, roughly in line with consolidated revenue growth (6.7%) -- SBC is NOT growing faster than the business, unlike some hypergrowth names, though buybacks only just cover it (uncovered_dilution near zero, not comfortably negative).

base.description: Consolidated ops: modest revenue growth (Telenet stable, Wyre still ramping off small base, VM Ireland slightly declining), EBITDA margin recovering from 20.8% (FY2025) toward ~26% as corporate costs fall ~75% by 2026 and Wyre/Telenet MSA reset benefits flow through; capex intensity falling from 27.5% of revenue (FY2025 Wyre peak) toward ~18% as fiber buildout matures -- Telenet alone guided to ~20% P&E/revenue in FY2026 (from ~38% FY2025). Cash tax rate low (5-15%) reflecting Bermuda 15% statutory rate and a $2.09B valuation allowance shielding most jurisdictions. JV stakes valued near current book/EV-EBITDA blend; Liberty Growth held flat at management's $3.4B FMV.
base.vmo2_stake_note: Blend of Q2-2026 equity-method carrying value ($3,481.1M) and EV/EBITDA cross-check (6.5x annualized EBITDA of ~£3.9B less ~5.0x-EBITDA net debt, 50% share, ~$3,745M).
base.vodafoneziggo_stake_note: Q2-2026 equity-method carrying value ($1,623.8M) used as the base-case anchor (no impairment recorded under equity-method testing).
base.liberty_growth_note: Management-reported FMV as of Q2-2026 ($3.4B across ~70 companies/funds), held flat -- already a mark-to-market figure, not projected.

bull.description: Faster FMC/B2B-driven revenue growth, EBITDA margin expansion to ~28.5% (corporate cost cuts land ahead of plan, Wyre/Telenet MSA synergies), capex falls faster to ~15% as fiber buildouts complete ahead of schedule. VMO2 re-rates toward a higher multiple on full-fiber/nexfibre optionality; VodafoneZiggo stake carries a ~35% premium for post-buyout control value and Ziggo Group 2027 spin-off synergy realization (~$1B stated synergies, ~€500M combined FCF target by 2028); Liberty Growth appreciates on AI/datacenter tailwinds and further high-IRR exits (EdgeConneX precedent: >30% IRR).

bear.description: Continued subscriber attrition (broadband/fixed-line net losses persisting across VMO2, Telenet, VM Ireland) pressures revenue slightly negative in early years; EBITDA margin compresses/stagnates around 20-22%; capex intensity stays elevated (defensive fiber spend) only gradually easing to ~20.5%. VMO2/VodafoneZiggo stakes marked down for competitive/execution risk; Liberty Growth portfolio marked down 20% for weaker exit markets.

bear.note: Bear case equity value is negative -- reflects genuine leverage risk: consolidated net debt ($5,931.7M) plus the VodafoneZiggo deal cash cost ($1,160M) exceed the heavily-discounted sum-of-parts asset value in a structural-decline scenario. This is not a modeling error; it is the bear case's core message -- LBTYA's equity is a leveraged call option on the JV stakes and Liberty Growth portfolio, and a genuinely adverse operating scenario combined with elevated opco leverage can wipe out most or all of the residual equity value.

entry_price.methodology_note: Entry price = price at which buying today, collecting projected interim consolidated-ops FCF plus JV cash distributions, and exiting at the year-5 sum-of-parts equity value earns a 15% IRR. A 5-year (not 10-year) horizon is used for entry-price purposes because JV stakes and the Liberty Growth portfolio are ALREADY marked at current fair/book value (not compounding growth assets requiring a full 10-year DCF); only the consolidated-ops component genuinely needs the longer horizon to reach a mature margin (used for the intrinsic-value calculation above).

base.pv_interim_cf_note: Sum of (consolidated ops owner FCF + VMO2 distributions [~$128M/yr flat] + VodafoneZiggo distributions [$0 FY26-27, resuming modestly $30-60M by Y3-5]) for Y1-5, discounted at 15%. Negative because consolidated ops FCF is still negative in Y1-Y2 of the capex-normalization path.
base.entry_price_note: Base case: NO price satisfies a 15% IRR hurdle over a 5-year horizon given current leverage and the still-negative near-term consolidated FCF -- the computed entry price is negative. This is directionally consistent with the base-case intrinsic value ($8.61) already sitting BELOW the current price ($10.61): the stock does not clear even its WACC-based (9.5%) hurdle in the base case, so it cannot clear the higher 15% hurdle either. Floor for display purposes: treat as 'no entry price / base case does not clear 15% IRR at any price >= $0'.

bull.interpretation: In the bull scenario, the current price ($10.61) is already BELOW the 15%-IRR entry price ($12.91) -- i.e., if VMO2/VodafoneZiggo turnarounds, Ziggo Group synergies, and Liberty Growth appreciation all play out as guided, buying today clears a 15% IRR with room to spare.

sensitivity.description: Base-case intrinsic value sensitivity to consolidated-ops WACC and terminal growth rate (JV stakes and Liberty Growth portfolio held constant at base-case values across the matrix).

probability_weighted.rationale: Base 50% (most likely: gradual consolidated-ops capex normalization, JV stakes roughly hold current value, Liberty Growth flat). Bull 30% (Ziggo Group 2027 spin-off and VodafoneZiggo turnaround are concrete, management-committed catalysts with a credible precedent in the value-accretive Sunrise 2024 spin-off, but multiple sequential execution/regulatory steps remain). Bear 20% (structural fiber-overbuild subscriber attrition is real and persistent across all opcos, and elevated opco-level leverage, 3.3-6.1x depending on entity, creates genuine equity-impairment tail risk in a downside scenario).

key_risks_to_valuation: VodafoneZiggo transaction execution: the ~$1.16B cash consideration is a near-certain near-term outflow (deal expected to close end-July 2026 per the Q2-2026 earnings call), but the ~$1B of stated synergies and the 2027 Ziggo Group Euronext spin-off require successful capital-structure separation, regulatory sign-off, and a receptive listing market -- none of which is underwritten in the base case.

Opco-level leverage is elevated and uneven (VMO2 4.4-5.9x, VodafoneZiggo 5.2-6.1x, VM Ireland 5.5-5.8x, Telenet 3.3-4.4x depending on covenant definition) -- the bear case shows this leverage can push consolidated equity value negative if operating performance deteriorates and JV/Growth marks compress simultaneously.

Structural fixed-line/broadband subscriber attrition persists at nearly every operating company (VMO2 consumer broadband -28,200 QoQ, Telenet fixed-line relationships -14,000 QoQ, VM Ireland broadband -5,000 QoQ in Q2 2026) despite heavy capex -- the consolidated-ops component's margin recovery assumes this moderates, which is guided but not guaranteed.

Buyback capacity has been sharply curtailed in 2026 ($0 in Q1, only a $200M authorization since July 2026, versus a multi-year multi-billion-dollar prior program) as capital is redirected to the VodafoneZiggo buy-in and deleveraging -- share count is assumed flat in this model, but if buybacks lag SBC in future years, uncovered dilution would re-emerge.

JV stake valuations rely on assumed net-debt/EBITDA multiples and EV/EBITDA multiples for VMO2 and VodafoneZiggo since neither is separately publicly listed; the base case blends an EV/EBITDA-derived estimate with Liberty Global's own equity-method carrying value as a sanity check, but both carry material estimation uncertainty.

Liberty Growth portfolio ($3.4B FMV) is management-marked and concentrated (top 5 holdings >50% of FMV after the EdgeConneX exit) -- private-market marks can be stale or optimistic relative to eventual exit proceeds.
Currency exposure: LBTYA reports in USD while nearly all economics are earned in EUR/GBP; a stronger dollar mechanically reduces USD-translated JV and consolidated-ops values.

implied_multiples.pe_note: n/m -- FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS is -$21.35 (JV impairments/fair-value losses), P/E not meaningful

historical_averages_ex_outliers.outliers_excluded: P/E history is not usable: positive-EPS years (FY2019, FY2021, FY2022, FY2024) were inflated by one-off disposal/JV gains giving absurd 0.6-3.7x ratios; all other years negative. P/B pre-FY2019 reflects a different consolidation perimeter (incl. UK/Swiss ops). EV/EBITDA on consolidated EBITDA is perimeter-inconsistent before FY2022 (Sunrise-restated years) -- post-2022 range is 12.2-16.8x because market cap embeds the equity-method VMO2/VodafoneZiggo stakes that contribute no consolidated EBITDA.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base-case IV $8.61 sits BELOW the current price (-18.8% upside) and implies P/B 0.30x vs 10yr max 2.45x and EV/EBITDA 11.2x vs post-restatement historical range 12.2-16.8x. The sum-of-the-parts base case is conservative relative to every multiple the market has actually paid.
sanity_check.methodology_note: Multiples are SBC-adjusted on both sides per workflow (EBITDA - SBC; EPS - SBC/share) and will NOT match Yahoo/screener GAAP figures. Implied EV/EBITDA compares total equity IV (incl. JV stakes) against consolidated EBITDA only -- the same asymmetry present in the historical market multiples, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.
